The Auditor-General's report on the 2024 financial year says most local authorities did not have ERP systems to manage revenue collection and most of their business processes were still manual or partially automated; some accounting-system modules were not activated.

The report, covering 89 local authorities, gives 'most' as the number without an ERP for revenue and lists no count or share with a revenue system; it also finds incomplete or outdated databases for revenue streams and non-billing of customers.

The Auditor-General reports that at Gwanda Municipality 27 stands sold in 2019 were still not being billed and the valuation roll was not yet finalised, which shows a billing record of stands that is incomplete.
The Harare Institute of Technology says its InstaPark parking management system is in use in 15 municipalities, with no total of municipalities given.
HIT says InstaPark lets councils collect 100 percent of parking revenue directly instead of through joint ventures with foreign firms; no register of payers is described.
HIT told the Harare Commission of Inquiry that around 83 of Zimbabwe's 92 local authorities use at least one LADS module; which modules, and whether any records revenue, is not stated.
HIT says LADS links local authorities' services, including financials and billing, to the national public financial management system.
The Deputy Minister of Local Government and Public Works said LADS will soon become a Strategic Business Unit of her ministry, with HIT as consultant.

The Deputy Minister said further LADS development will be funded through a Devolution Operational Grant from government, so local authorities stop paying annual licences once funds are directed to HIT.

CLGF reports the City of Mutare's Finance Department runs LADS debt management, procurement and budgeting modules, and that its revenue collection rose from 35% to nearly 72%; the document gives no date for the change.
CLGF says LADS was initially rolled out to six local authorities, with a roll-out to all local authorities under way; the document dates neither, so its publication date is used.
CLGF, with the Harare Institute of Technology and the Ministry of Local Government, rolled out LADS to its first six local authorities.
CLGF says the LADS roll-out came with capacity building and technical and financial support to the local authorities.
